title: Fairness
competency: Define and apply fairness when dealing with others.

keywords.def: Judging people and situations without bias, giving everyone a fair chance based on merit and ability.

en.text: Fairness is judging without bias and giving everyone a chance to benefit. It means treating people equitably by merit and ability, handling similar cases the same way, and deciding by proper criteria without favouritism. Fair does not always mean exactly the same for everyone.

am.text: ፍትሐዊነት ያለ አድልዎ መፍረድና ለሁሉም ዕድል መስጠት ነው። ፍትሐዊ ማለት ሁልጊዜ ለሁሉም አንድ ዓይነት ማለት አይደለም።

screens.title: The class prize
screens.ask: A teacher gives the class prize to her neighbour's son, though another student scored higher. Is it fair?
opts: No: the decision was based on favouritism
screens.after: Not fair. Fairness bases decisions on merit, free of favouritism.

screens.title: Fairness
paras: Fairness is treating people fairly and not letting personal feelings decide.
It evaluates people and situations without bias.
Everyone in a group should have a chance to benefit.
Being fair does not always mean treating everyone the same way in every situation.
screens.note: Fairness requires: treat people equitably by merit and ability; handle similar situations similarly; decide by proper criteria, free of favouritism or prejudice.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Judging people and situations without bias, giving everyone a fair chance based on merit and ability.

screens.text: A student with poor eyesight gets a front seat. Others say "unfair!" Who is right?

screens.ans: The teacher: fairness can mean different treatment for different needs
